subsystems.name: Agent runtime
subsystems.role: runs one agent: a model plus its tools and local memory.

subsystems.name: Orchestrator
subsystems.role: decomposes a goal into subtasks and assigns them to agents.

subsystems.name: Communication fabric
subsystems.role: lets agents share results and state without stepping on each other.

subsystems.name: Memory
subsystems.role: stores shared knowledge and each agent's history across steps.

subsystems.name: Tool layer
subsystems.role: connects agents to external systems so they can act.

subsystems.name: Safety and oversight
subsystems.role: keeps the swarm within bounds and lets humans intervene.

buildSteps.title: Define the goal and decomposition
buildSteps.detail: Specify success criteria and the top-level tasks that can be split among agents.

buildSteps.title: Choose the agent population
buildSteps.detail: Decide how many agents, what roles they play, and whether they share one model or use specialised ones.

buildSteps.title: Build the communication substrate
buildSteps.detail: Set up a shared blackboard or message bus so agents can post partial results and read others' work.

buildSteps.title: Implement the planner
buildSteps.detail: Write a recursive task decomposer that breaks goals into subtasks and assigns them.

buildSteps.title: Give agents tools
buildSteps.detail: Connect APIs, code interpreters and search so agents can act on the world.

buildSteps.title: Add memory
buildSteps.detail: Store short-term context and long-term results in a vector database or structured log.

buildSteps.title: Define coordination rules
buildSteps.detail: Choose how agents negotiate, vote, or follow a hierarchy to merge results and resolve conflicts.

buildSteps.title: Train or prompt
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune models on multi-agent traces or use detailed role prompts with few-shot examples.

buildSteps.title: Test and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Run in simulation, then in a sandbox with human oversight before any autonomous operation.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with reliable reasoning
prerequisites.why: they can plan and use tools, but long-horizon reliability is unproven.
research shows coordination can emerge, but it is fragile and sample-hungry.
agents need safe ways to call APIs and run code.
swarms generate far more state than a single model can hold.
no proven way to guarantee a swarm of agents will stay on task and within limits.

pathway.milestone: single AI assistants with tool use
small agent teams for coding and research with human review
orchestrators for enterprise workflows with audit trails
open-ended swarms tackling novel problems with minimal oversight
pathway.unlocks: scientific discovery and complex logistics — if safety and reliability are solved.
